posts.title: Book Review: Taking Flight
posts.description: Taking Flight by K. Scriven is a fun fantasy adventure about family, pursuing your dreams and embracing who you are. I thoroughly enjoyed this first instalment of Sira’s story, which introduces us to a world that’s a fascinating mashup of steampunk, fae and mages. Sira is a feisty young woman who has rejected her magical heritage in favour of training to fly airships. But she soon gets stranded in the forest with a celebrated young mage and embroiled in a dangerous plot that sees her fighting for both their lives. I loved how the author gradually revealed Sira’s history — her strained relationship with her twin brother, the tragedy of her deceased parents — which shaped her into the person she is at the beginning of the novel. Sira’s inner arc in this book deals with her coming to terms with these familial relationships and her attitude to magic in general. There’s also a teeny bit of a romantic subplot between Sira and James as they fight together for survival. Overall, Taking Flight

posts.title: Book Review: The Silent Paths of Night
posts.description: The Silent Paths of Night by David R Slayton is the wonderful sequel to the equally wonderful Dark Moon Shallow Sea . I’m loving this Gods of Night and Day epic fantasy series — and there’s more to come. Yay! These books have just the right blend of character, adventure and lore/worldbuilding. They are intimate, exciting, hopeful (even when things get dark), and laced with all kinds of love. They are going straight into my favourites list, and I’ll be re-reading (listening) to them for years to come. Being book 2, The Silent Paths of Night picks up several months after Dark Moon Shallow Sea . The latter ended in a good place and could be read as a standalone, but this second book feels more like a “part 1” of the next phase of Seth and Raef’s adventure and ends with a revelation that feels like a cliffhanger. (That said, you absolutely must read Dark Moon first.) In the time between the books, Seth and Raef have completed a bunch of errands (tied up loose ends) leftover from the first

posts.title: Book Review: A Bond of Thread
posts.description: I thoroughly enjoyed A Bond of Thread by Allegra Pescatore and JP Burnison — a romantic fantasy about a Faerie Queen, Skye, who is running from her destiny, and a winged Fae warrior, Ilyas, hiding from his past. They’re reluctantly forced together through circumstance and help a village to repel a horde of “ferals” (essentially fae monsters) after the villagers are driven into some caves. My favourite thing about this book was the wonderful “fair folk” — comprising skitterlings (tiny winged fairies), druzies (made of rock crystals) and the tree-like mosskin — who live alongside the High Fae. They’re treated like second class citizens/slaves, but Skye shows everyone how wonderful and important the fair folk are — especially the tiny and incurably frank skitterling, Mycellica. She’s fabulous, flying about trying to help Ilyas and Skye along in their relationship.
